chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The father is the only one who annuls the marriage.'
ai.seo_question: Who has the authority to annul the marriage of a virgin daughter according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Isfahani establishes the exclusive authority of the father (al-ab) in validating or annulling the marriage contract of his virgin daughter, a ruling central to Shia jurisprudence. While some schools include the mother, this narration emphasizes the paternal guardianship (wilayah) as the decisive factor for the validity of the nuptial bond. It underscores the father's role as the primary legal guardian in family matters, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on paternal consent for a virgin's marriage.
